c048.front: What does DDL do with an open transaction?
c048.back: It commits it (COMMIT) by itself, before and after the DDL statement. Even DDL that fails during execution (for example ORA-00955, name already used) still commits. A syntax error does not commit. All savepoints disappear.

c049.front: TRUNCATE or DELETE: how do they differ?
c049.back: TRUNCATE is DDL: it cannot be undone with ROLLBACK, it does not fire DML triggers, and it resets the high-water mark. DELETE is DML: it writes undo, fires triggers, and can be undone with ROLLBACK.

c050.back: ALL: inserts for every WHEN that is true. FIRST: only for the first true WHEN, and checks no further. INSERT ALL without WHEN inserts into every INTO.

c051.back: You cannot change the columns used in ON (ORA-38104). Every WHEN clause is optional. In WHEN MATCHED you can add DELETE WHERE.
c051.try_sql:
-- A column from ON in UPDATE SET: error
MERGE INTO departments d
USING (SELECT 10 AS id FROM dual) s
ON (d.department_id = s.id)
WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET d.department_id = 11;

c052.front: What does ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT do?
c052.back: It undoes the changes made after the savepoint. Earlier changes stay, and the transaction goes on. Savepoints created later disappear.

c053.front: Readers and writers: who blocks whom?
c053.back: Readers never block writers and see only committed data (read consistency). Writers block each other only on the same row.

c054.front: What does SELECT ... FOR UPDATE do?
c054.back: It locks the selected rows until COMMIT/ROLLBACK. NOWAIT / WAIT n say how long to wait for a locked row. COMMIT releases the locks.

c500.front: INSERT: what do the columns missing from the column list get?
c500.back: Their DEFAULT value, or NULL if there is none. A NOT NULL column without DEFAULT raises ORA-01400. Without a column list, VALUES must give a value for every column, in table order (otherwise ORA-00947).

c501.front: UPDATE ... SET col = (subquery): what if the subquery returns zero rows? And two?
c501.back: Zero rows: the column gets NULL. More than one row: ORA-01427. The subquery sees the data as it was at the start of the statement.

c502.front: One statement in a transaction fails. What is rolled back?
c502.back: Only that one statement (statement-level rollback). Earlier changes still wait for COMMIT, and the transaction goes on.

c503.front: MERGE ... UPDATE SET ... DELETE WHERE cond: which rows can be deleted?
c503.back: Only target rows changed by this MERGE, tested with their new values. Rows without a match are never deleted. A row matched twice: ORA-30926.

c504.front: TRUNCATE of a parent table that a foreign key points to?
c504.back: ORA-02266, as long as child rows point to it through an enabled FK (in 19c it went through when the child table was empty). TRUNCATE ... CASCADE (12c+) also clears the children, but only when the FKs are ON DELETE CASCADE (otherwise ORA-14705).

c505.front: What restrictions does a multitable INSERT have?
c505.back: The target cannot be a view or a remote table. You cannot use a sequence in the subquery. INSERT FIRST always needs WHEN. ELSE exists only in the conditional version (with WHEN).
c505.try_sql:
-- INSERT FIRST without WHEN: syntax error
INSERT FIRST
  INTO promotions VALUES (1, 'A', 5)
SELECT * FROM dual;

c1500.front: Multitable INSERT: which columns can WHEN and VALUES use?
c1500.back: Only columns (or column aliases) from the subquery's SELECT list. A table column you did not select, or a table alias like e.salary, raises ORA-00904.
c1500.try_sql:
-- salary is not in the subquery's SELECT list: ORA-00904
INSERT ALL
  WHEN salary > 10000 THEN INTO promotions VALUES (employee_id, last_name, 10)
SELECT employee_id, last_name FROM employees;

c1501.front: How do you insert several rows of literals with one statement?
c1501.back: 19c: INSERT ALL INTO t VALUES (...) INTO t VALUES (...) SELECT * FROM dual, or INSERT INTO t SELECT ... FROM dual UNION ALL SELECT ... FROM dual. 23ai also allows VALUES (...), (...) (on 19c that is ORA-00933).

c1502.front: One row of a multitable INSERT breaks a constraint. What remains?
c1502.back: Nothing from that statement: it is one statement, so it rolls back as a whole (statement-level rollback). Earlier statements of the transaction still wait for COMMIT.

c1503.front: WHEN x < 100 ... WHEN x >= 100 ... ELSE ...: when does ELSE apply?
c1503.back: When no WHEN is TRUE. That is also the case for x IS NULL, because both conditions give UNKNOWN. ELSE may be used in a conditional INSERT ALL and in INSERT FIRST.
c1503.try_sql:
-- x is NULL: both WHENs give UNKNOWN, the row goes to ELSE
INSERT FIRST
  WHEN x < 100 THEN INTO promotions VALUES (1, 'mniej', x)
  WHEN x >= 100 THEN INTO promotions VALUES (2, 'wiecej', x)
  ELSE INTO promotions VALUES (3, 'ELSE', x)
SELECT CAST(NULL AS NUMBER) AS x FROM dual;
SELECT * FROM promotions;

c1504.front: MERGE ... ON (1 = 0): what does it give?
c1504.back: No row ever matches, so every source row goes to WHEN NOT MATCHED. The MERGE then works like INSERT ... SELECT.
c1504.try_sql:
-- ON (1 = 0): department 10 exists, but it still goes to INSERT (ORA-00001)
MERGE INTO departments d
USING (SELECT 10 AS id, 'Admin 2' AS name FROM dual) s
ON (1 = 0)
WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET d.department_name = s.name
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (department_id, department_name) VALUES (s.id, s.name);

c1505.front: MERGE: the ON condition compares two NULLs. Matched or not?
c1505.back: Not matched. NULL = NULL is UNKNOWN, not TRUE. The row goes to the INSERT branch and can raise ORA-00001 if that key already exists.
c1505.try_sql:
-- Hooli (5) has country_code NULL: NULL = NULL does not match, so INSERT and ORA-00001
MERGE INTO customers c
USING (SELECT 5 AS id, 'Hooli' AS name, CAST(NULL AS CHAR(2)) AS cc FROM dual) s
ON (c.customer_id = s.id AND c.country_code = s.cc)
WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET c.credit_limit = 0
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (customer_id, customer_name) VALUES (s.id, s.name);

c1506.front: MERGE: UPDATE SET ... WHERE cond1 DELETE WHERE cond2. Which rows can be deleted?
c1506.back: Only matched rows that passed cond1 and were updated. cond2 already sees the new values. A row skipped by the UPDATE's WHERE is never deleted.
c1506.try_sql:
-- Line 2 (price 25) matches DELETE WHERE, but the UPDATE's WHERE skipped it: it stays
MERGE INTO order_items t
USING (SELECT 1001 AS oid FROM dual) s
ON (t.order_id = s.oid)
WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET t.unit_price = t.unit_price WHERE t.line_no = 1
  DELETE WHERE t.unit_price < 2000;
SELECT order_id, line_no, unit_price FROM order_items WHERE order_id = 1001;

c1507.front: Can WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE WHERE ... stand on its own?
c1507.back: No. DELETE WHERE is part of the UPDATE branch: WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET ... DELETE WHERE ... (without UPDATE: ORA-00905 on 19c, ORA-02000 on 23ai).
c1507.try_sql:
-- WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE without UPDATE: syntax error
MERGE INTO order_items t
USING (SELECT 1001 AS oid FROM dual) s
ON (t.order_id = s.oid)
WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE WHERE t.unit_price < 100;

c1508.front: Can you ROLLBACK TO the same savepoint twice?
c1508.back: Yes. ROLLBACK TO s keeps s (only later savepoints disappear), so a second ROLLBACK TO s works and undoes what you did since the first.

c1509.back: It releases the locks taken after the savepoint (another session can then lock that row). Locks from before the savepoint stay until COMMIT or ROLLBACK.

c1510.front: FOR UPDATE NOWAIT / WAIT n on a locked row?
c1510.back: NOWAIT: ORA-00054 at once. WAIT n: waits n seconds, then ORA-30006 on 19c (ORA-00054 on 23ai). Without either, it waits forever.

c1511.front: Does DDL that ended with an error still commit?
c1511.back: Yes, if it failed during execution: TRUNCATE of a missing table (ORA-00942) or CREATE with a name already in use (ORA-00955) first commits the pending DML. A syntax error does not commit. In 23ai DDL with IF [NOT] EXISTS that does nothing also commits.
